messages:
elena-cs: heads up — a customer (acme-ml) opened a severity-2 about embedding p99s in us-west-2, started ~03:10 UTC after our maintenance window. says p95 also drifted from 120ms -> 450ms.
ben-oncall: thanks. any correlation with the CUDA/driver rollout we did last night? which hosts affected?
elena-cs: customer call logs show spike starting at 03:08. they hit the embeddings endpoint (embeddings.v1) at ~500rps. support-bot: attached customerTimeline.csv and quick HAR.
carla-eng-infra: we did roll CUDA 13.1 + firmware to the usw2-gpu pool at 02:45–03:15. I saw elevated nvme write latency on a subset of nodes during the rollout window. pulling dmesg now.
dave-sre: can someone grab iostat -x, nvme top, and /proc/interrupts during a spike? also need kernel tracing (bpftrace one-liners) and the runtime's token throughput logs.
elena-cs: customer provided one sample request id: req_0a7b3c, attached to thread. they said lowering concurrency helped temporarily.
carla-eng-infra: snippet from dmesg on host-gpu-12: "nvme nvme0: timeout (completion) - resetting controller" and binder warnings. also saw IO scheduler stacking up io_queued.
ben-oncall: that matches host-level nvme stalls causing reactor stalls in the runtime. raj-mlops, does runtime fallback to CPU model variant when GPU queueing grows? any backpressure?
raj-mlops: runtime does backpressure but KV cache flushes can cause short high tail. we don't currently throttle NVMe flush concurrency aggressively. we do have a fallback to smaller batch sizes but it requires a warmup.
dave-sre: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily pin traffic for affected customers to gpu-pool-b (older driver) via routing rules, 2) throttle storage flush concurrency by setting ENV FLUSH_CONCURRENCY=4 on inference workers, 3) rollback driver on a small canary set if necessary. can infra enact 1 and 2?
carla-eng-infra: enacting step 2 now on usab-rtpool: set FLUSH_CONCURRENCY=4 via nomad update; also patched cgroup blkio.throttle.write_bps_device for nvme0 to 200MB/s on two nodes.
ben-oncall: pushing a routing tweak to pin acme-ml to gp-old via route override for the customer token. deploy-bot: route override applied for token acme-xxxx -> gp-old (effective immediate).
elena-cs: customer confirmed latency dropped to p95 ~180ms after routing change and throttle. they're still seeing occasional p99 blips ~700ms but much better. :thumbsup:
raj-mlops: we'll add a short-term change to aggressively reduce batch size on GPUs with >30% IO wait and add a KV cache backoff. I'll open a PR with the runtime knobs.
dave-sre: follow-ups: 1) infra to bisect firmware/driver combo across hosts (carla), 2) eng to add IO-aware backoff + metrics in runtime (raj), 3) CS to keep customer updated (elena).
carla-eng-infra: starting bisect: will roll driver/firmware combinations on a canary pool overnight and run synthetic embedding load to reproduce. collecting nvme SMART and fio profiles.
elena-cs: scheduled customer follow-up at 09:00 PT. will share monitoring dashboard and p95/p99 deltas.
ben-oncall: nice quick mitigation. mark this thread as in-progress — escalate to eng on-call for bisect if we see reappearance after next rollout.
support-bot: incident-3618901234: actions taken: route-override, FLUSH_CONCURRENCY set, blkio throttle set on 2 nodes, canary bisect scheduled.
carla-eng-infra: discovered correlation: hosts with older nvme firmware + new CUDA driver show amplified driver-to-host interrupts causing long NVMe completions. suspect kernel-driver interaction. will open infra bug ticket with vendor dumps.
dave-sre: thanks. moving to monitoring-watch for 24h. please paste any repro scripts here.
raj-mlops: repro script: run ffmpeg-style parallel requests to embeddings with seq_len=2048 and embeddings batch=16; run fio randomrw 4k 32 jobs concurrently on nvme while measuring tail. posting gist: https://gist.internal/repro-3618901234
elena-cs: customer happy for now, keeping open until canary bisect completes. will update once they confirm stable p99. :white_check_mark:
